solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Verbally attack a burrowing rodent

indicators.note: verbally says the phrase meaning attack is spoken out loud, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: to go for someone is to attack them

explanation.surface: An instruction to shout abuse at a small animal that digs tunnels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Verbally' is the sound signal: 'go for' (attack) spoken out loud is the same as the name of the rodent.
explanation.definitionFit: The gopher is a North American rodent that lives in underground tunnels it digs itself.

clue.text: Elevated article about, say, a European port

indicators.note: elevated means raised, so in this down clue the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
on means about, concerning
eg, for example, means say

explanation.surface: An upmarket newspaper piece about a harbour city in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Genoa is the chief seaport of north-western Italy.

clue.text: Impecunious writer on river vessel

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
the Nile is the river of Egypt
SS, steamship, stands for a vessel

explanation.surface: A poor author is travelling on a Nile cruise boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Penniless and impecunious both mean having no money.

clue.text: Brittle BBC boss in first of exacting years

indicators.note: in says the boss goes inside the other letters
first of says take the opening letter of exacting

parts.note: the head of the BBC is its Director-General, DG

explanation.surface: A tetchy head of the BBC spends his first years in a demanding job.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgy and brittle both describe someone tense and easily upset.

clue.text: Wilfully desire no more than …

parts.note: to desire is to want
no more than means only, as in only two left

explanation.surface: Wanting things on purpose and nothing more, trailing off into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs this clue's surface on into 10 across; it plays no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Wantonly describes acting deliberately and without restraint or cause, so wilfully is a synonym.

clue.text: Risk assessor's deed unknown by Egypt once

parts.note: a deed is an act
the United Arab Republic, UAR, was Egypt's official name from 1958 to 1971
y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: An insurance expert's action is not recognised by the old Egyptian state.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after the definition stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: An actuary calculates insurance risks and premiums from statistics.

clue.text: Some who spill the beans on joint position at bank

parts.note: tellers are people who tell, that is reveal secrets
the hip is a joint

explanation.surface: Gossipy people are chatting about a shared job at a bank.
explanation.definitionFit: A tellership is the post of a teller, a cashier who deals with customers in a bank.

clue.text: Worthy old law graduate in the Newcastle area

indicators.note: in says old and the graduate go inside the area

parts.note: Newcastle is in the north-east of England, NE
BL is a Bachelor of Law

explanation.surface: A deserving elderly law graduate lives in the north-east of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Noble means worthy, of high moral character.

clue.text: County fellow looking up at king on heavy horse

indicators.note: looking up means facing upwards, so in this down clue the name reads from bottom to top

parts.note: Roy is a man's name
k is the abbreviation for king in chess
the shire is a breed of heavy draught horse

explanation.surface: A man gazes up at a king mounted on a great carthorse.
explanation.definitionFit: Yorkshire is the largest historic county of England.

clue.text: Involve Irish leader in hire charge right away

indicators.note: in says the Irish leader goes inside what is left
right away says the r, for right, is taken out

parts.note: a rental is a charge for hiring

indicators.note: leader says take the first letter of Irish

explanation.surface: An Irish prime minister gets caught up in a hire fee immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' removes R from RENTAL, leaving ENTAL, and the I goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: To entail something is to involve it as a necessary consequence.

clue.text: … some information on a Gonzalez figure

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Continuing 4 across: someone wants only a little information about a person named Gonzalez.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonagon is a nine-sided polygon, and a polygon is a geometrical figure.

clue.text: Ring pub, finding obstruction on the way

parts.note: to ring a bell is to toll it
a bar is a pub or the counter in one

explanation.surface: Phone the local and learn that the road is blocked.
explanation.definitionFit: A tollbar is a barrier across a road where travellers must stop to pay a charge.

clue.text: Mine entrance required: reportedly do this, then?

indicators.note: reportedly says the instruction is to be heard rather than read, giving a word sounding the same

parts.note: the thing to do when something is required is add it

explanation.surface: A puzzled note: a way into a mine is needed, so presumably one should do this?
explanation.walkthrough: If something is required, you 'add it'; said out loud that phrase gives the mining term.
explanation.definitionFit: An adit is a horizontal passage driven into a hillside to give access to or drain a mine.

clue.text: Supervisor taking a horse with hesitation into eating-place

indicators.note: into says the horse and the hesitation are placed inside the eating-place

parts.note: a mess is a place where soldiers or sailors eat together
a nag is an old horse
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A boss leads a horse, pausing, into a canteen.
explanation.definitionFit: A manageress is a woman in charge of a shop, restaurant or similar business: a supervisor.

clue.text: Loiter in half of London street with key accomplice

indicators.note: half of says only the back half of the street's name is kept

parts.note: Piccadilly is a famous street in London's West End
D is a musical key
an ally is a helper or accomplice

explanation.surface: Hanging about on a London thoroughfare with a fellow conspirator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' keeps the second half of PICCADILLY, DILLY.
explanation.definitionFit: To dilly-dally is to waste time or dawdle, which is to loiter.

clue.text: Girl crossing quiet City area for a particular purpose

indicators.note: the girl's name crosses, or spans, the quiet and the area, holding them inside

parts.note: Sally is a girl's name
p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
EC1 is a postcode district of the City of London, its 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A young woman walks across a calm part of the City of London.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district; its postcodes start EC, and EC1 doubles as ECI.
explanation.definitionFit: Specially means for one special purpose, as in a cake made specially for the party.

clue.text: Shortly request a time to enter Canadian city

indicators.note: to enter says these letters go inside the word for shortly

parts.note: soon means shortly
to request is to ask

explanation.surface: A brief plea for an appointment to visit a city in Canada.
explanation.definitionFit: Saskatoon is the largest city in the Canadian province of Saskatchewan.

clue.text: Retired American cooking his Japanese dish

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the letters for American are read backwards
cooking says the letters of his are being worked into a new form

explanation.surface: A retired man from the US prepares a Japanese meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' turns US into SU; 'cooking' rearranges HIS into SHI.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is a Japanese dish of vinegared rice topped or rolled with raw fish and other ingredients.

clue.text: Loose pig that's beginning to eat human food

indicators.note: loose means let free, so these letters are set loose into a new order
beginning to says take the first letter of eat

explanation.surface: An escaped pig starts tucking into people's dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaghetti is a long thin pasta, a staple food for people rather than pigs.

clue.text: Fibre I recognised in girl from the East

indicators.note: recognised in says the letter I is seen inside the girl
from the East means read from right to left, as east is on the right of a map

parts.note: a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: Someone spots a kind of fibre in a young woman who has come from Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the East' turns LASS into SSAL, and I goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisal is a stiff plant fibre from an agave, used to make rope and matting.

clue.text: M Hulot's creator backed in serious move

indicators.note: in says the backed name sits inside the word for serious

parts.note: grave means serious

indicators.note: backed means reversed, so the creator's name runs backwards

parts.note: Jacques Tati, the French film-maker, created and played Monsieur Hulot

explanation.surface: Backing Monsieur Hulot's creator in a solemn step, like a film financier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns TATI into ITAT, which goes into GRAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To gravitate is to move or be drawn towards something, as if by gravity.

clue.text: Man framing Burlington House member's "Sea creature"

indicators.note: framing means surrounding, so the man's name goes round the rest

parts.note: Gus is a man's name
Burlington House in London is home of the Royal Academy, RA
MP, Member of Parliament, is a member

explanation.surface: A man frames the title of a painting by a Royal Academician.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Academy is based at Burlington House on Piccadilly.
explanation.definitionFit: Grampus is an old name for Risso's dolphin or the killer whale, sea-dwelling animals.

clue.text: A male animal finally loaded on ship

parts.note: a boar is a male pig

indicators.note: finally says take the last letter of loaded

explanation.surface: A boar is the last thing to be loaded onto a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Aboard means on or onto a ship or other vessel.

clue.text: Priest and waggish faculty head keeping company

parts.note: arch means playfully mischievous or knowing

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so the faculty head holds the company inside

parts.note: a dean heads a university faculty

explanation.surface: A cleric and a jokey university dean spend time together.
explanation.definitionFit: An archdeacon is a senior Anglican cleric ranking just below a bishop, so a priest.

clue.text: Pick of elkhounds originally in pack

indicators.note: in says the first letter goes inside the word for pack

parts.note: to pack is to cram

indicators.note: originally says take the opening letter of elkhounds

explanation.surface: Choosing the best of the elkhounds from a pack of dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pick' looks like a verb but is a noun, the pick of the bunch.
explanation.definitionFit: The cream of something is its best part, as the pick of it is.

clue.text: Stylish around here in ancient Rome?

parts.note: c, for circa, means around, as with dates
hic is the Latin word for here

explanation.surface: Asking whether fashion was found hereabouts in the days of the Roman Empire.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic means elegantly fashionable, a synonym of stylish.

clue.text: Endless task overwhelming current group of singers

indicators.note: overwhelming means covering over, so the shortened task goes round the current
endless says the final letter of the task is dropped

parts.note: a chore is a task
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: An unending job swamps the electricity supply for a choral group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' cuts CHORE to CHOR, which goes round I.
explanation.definitionFit: A choir is an organised body of singers.

clue.text: Capital city's extremists fleeing industrial action

indicators.note: extremists fleeing says the letters at both extremes run off

parts.note: a go-slow is a form of industrial action where workers deliberately work slowly

explanation.surface: Radicals run from a strike in a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremists fleeing' removes the G and W at the ends of GOSLOW. The 's after the definition stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Oslo is the capital city of Norway.

clue.text: Partly coincide — and drink too much!

parts.note: over means too much, as in overdo
to lap is to drink, as a cat does

explanation.surface: Two things nearly match, and someone goes overboard with the drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark flags the whimsical reading: the answer split in two gives 'drink too much'.
explanation.definitionFit: Things overlap when they partly cover each other, sharing some of the same ground.

clue.text: You cook it and soak it ultimately in port

indicators.note: in says the drinker and the final letter sit inside the port

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port
a soak is a heavy drinker, a sot

indicators.note: ultimately says take the last letter of the second it

explanation.surface: Instructions: prepare it and give it a long soaking while in harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soak' is not a verb here but a noun, a drunkard.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is an Italian rice dish that you cook slowly with stock, so it is something you cook.

clue.text: Belfast doctor maybe is involved with my opposition to local development

parts.note: Belfast is the capital of Northern Ireland, NI
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is one qualification of a doctor

indicators.note: involved means tangled, so the letters of is and my are mixed up

explanation.surface: A Northern Irish GP is caught up in the speaker's campaign against building nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: Nimbyism, from Not In My Back Yard, is objecting to new building or schemes near one's home.

clue.text: More glutinous tonic regularly swallowed by dynamic person

indicators.note: swallowed by says the picked letters go inside the dynamic person

parts.note: a goer is an energetic, go-ahead person

indicators.note: regularly says take every other letter of tonic

explanation.surface: A thicker tonic drink is gulped down by an energetic person.
explanation.definitionFit: Gooier means stickier and more like goo, which is glutinous.
